# Independent VeraCrypt compatibility corpus

`compatibility.json` holds 24 synthetic VeraCrypt and TrueCrypt containers and
the unlock checks `tests/compatibility.rs` runs on them. They are public test
data generated by this repository; no real evidence and no bytes of VeraCrypt
or cryptsetup images are included. They follow this vendored crate's Apache-2.0
license.

Generator: `scripts/make-veracrypt-compatibility-fixtures.py` at the
repository root. It writes XTS, the headers, keyfile mixing and every layout
itself on top of Python 3.10's hashlib/hmac (PBKDF2 over SHA-512, SHA-256,
BLAKE2s, Whirlpool, RIPEMD-160), cryptography 48.0.0 (AES, Camellia, Argon2id,
and OpenSSL AES-XTS as a check of its own XTS) and twofish 0.3.0. The Rust
reader is not used. The dependencies are needed only to regenerate:

```text
python scripts/make-veracrypt-compatibility-fixtures.py
just test-veracrypt
```

Passwords are UTF-8 `LovelyCarve-密码` (hidden volumes `hidden-密码`); the
keyfiles are stored in the corpus. A volume with seed `s` holds plaintext byte
`(i * 29 + s) mod 256` at offset `i`; master keys are
`(i * 73 + s) mod 256`. VeraCrypt counts use PIM 1 (16000 iterations, 2048 for
pre-boot SHA-256 / BLAKE2s, Argon2id 64 MiB × 3 passes) to keep the suite fast.

SHA-256 of the UTF-8 JSON with LF newlines:

`70def73616ec1c953b31a7b3bd45f56cd77a2e5c826b917ccf930ddd6cab703a`

Update the hash when intentionally changing the corpus. Serpent, Kuznyechik
and Streebog have no Python implementation here; VeraCrypt's own self-test
vectors in the unit tests cover them.
